key_idea: Each connected component of a bipartite graph has exactly 2 colourings, and swapping rooms globally is not a new assignment, so there are 2^(c-1) assignments and the answer is 2^(c-1)+1.
sketch: Check bipartiteness with a parity DSU (or BFS colouring) over n, m <= 1e6 and count components c, including isolated vertices. If an odd cycle exists print impossible; otherwise print (2^(c-1) + 1) mod p by pigeonhole. Near-linear time. Pitfalls: use an iterative find to avoid deep recursion on 1e6-long paths, p can be as small as 3 so reduce every step, and c-1 = 0 gives 2.
